title.narrative: UNFPA: Human Resources for SRH & GBV in South Sudan

description.narrative:
The project direct beneficiaries will include:
Women, girls and boys including pregnant women from targeted states who will use integrated SRHR, GBV and HIV services for better health outcomes
Health workers based at hospitals including midwives, doctors, associate clinicians, nurses, obstetricians, who will benefit from capacity building activities including in-service training and online courses. Health care providers including doctors, obstetricians, midwives and nurses will be provided with relevant incentives, on-the-job training on SRHR, GBV and HIV as well as training in rational use of reproductive health commodities, drugs and supplies.
Tutors at health sciences institutes who will develop their skills and abilities to provide courses with evidence-based approaches of integrated SRHR/GBV/HIV services.
Health facility managers and other relevant staff who will be trained to manage reproductive health drug supply and distribution, maintenance of equipment such as solar and water supply systems.
Data and administrative clerks and other officials who will be trained to collect and analyze service statistics.
Staff members of the various departments of the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Gender who will benefit directly from project activities through technical assistance, capacity building and support throughout the project period.
Community and traditional leaders who will benefit from training to be champions on gender equality at the community level
Service providers at the Family Protection Centre (or the one-stop centres for GBV survivors) who will be trained to provide client-centered services to GBV survivors.

The project will focus on four key components:
Strengthening the provision of quality integrated SRH/GBV/HIV services. Increasing awareness among women, girls, men, and boys to utilize gender responsive SRH/GBV/HIV services. Strengthening health training institutions to produced quality human resources for SRHR/GBV/HIV services; and Improving national and state government capacities to develop and implement SRH/GBV/HIV policies, legislations, and coordination mechanisms

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every birth is safe, and every young person's potential is fulfilled. In South Sudan, UNFPA works with the government and other partners to ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights and contribute to the following transformative results:
End preventable maternal deaths End the unmet need for family planning End gender-based violence and all harmful practices, including child marriage End new HIV infections among young people
This is enabled by evidence and population expertise, focusing on empowerment of women and young people, especially adolescent girls, and delivered in both humanitarian and development settings
